purpose: Section 12-15 remediation (extended this sprint, Gate 3 closure): the single, explicit governance registry for current Stage-3 scientific evidence. Every artifact referenced anywhere in the Stage-3 governance layer must have an explicit registry status here - governance is NEVER inferred from filename or key-name substrings. Beyond the registry-level status, GOVERNING resolution additionally requires the artifact's OWN machine-readable content to independently corroborate governance-eligibility - see 'artifact_status_contract' below. This defends against the specific attack of flipping one registry status field without the underlying artifact supporting that claim. ml/stage3_science_resolver.py is the only code path that should be used to resolve 'the current governing result' for a family.
rule: Within a family, exactly one artifact may have status GOVERNING. HISTORICAL, SUPERSEDED, INVALIDATED, NONCANONICAL_REPRODUCTION, and PENDING artifacts may never be treated as governing regardless of key name or position in this file.

artifact_status_contract.purpose: For every artifact, declares WHERE the resolver should independently read that artifact's own semantic status from, so a registry-level GOVERNING label alone is never sufficient. 'status_field' names a top-level JSON key in the artifact itself that the resolver re-reads live at resolution time; if present and its value contains a forbidden marker (see forbidden_semantic_markers), resolution fails regardless of the registry's declared status. 'artifact_semantic_status' is used ONLY when the artifact has no natural status-bearing field - it is a registry-asserted fallback, explicitly weaker (a determined attacker who controls the registry could still forge it), and is disclosed as such rather than presented as equivalent to a live field read.
